name: Toggle
description: A binary on/off switch rendered as a styled checkbox with role='switch'. The thumb position (not colour alone) communicates the checked state. Integrates with FormControl context to receive id, disabled, and required state automatically.

notes: The underlying input has type='checkbox' and role='switch' — assistive technology announces on/off state via aria-checked.
Thumb position is the primary non-color indicator: off = inline-start, on = inline-end.
Focus indicator is a 2px solid outline on the track using var(--color-border-focus) with a 2px offset.
Disabled state reduces opacity and sets cursor: not-allowed.
prefers-reduced-motion is respected — transition is disabled when the user has opted out of motion.
Touch target meets 44x44px minimum for the md size via min-block-size on the label wrapper.

checked.description: Whether the toggle is in the on (checked) state. Use with onChange for controlled usage.

defaultChecked.description: Initial checked state for uncontrolled usage.

disabled.description: Disables the toggle. Also inherited from FormControl context if not explicitly set.

onChange.description: Callback fired when the checked state changes.

children.description: Optional label text rendered beside the track.

size.description: Size variant. xs renders the smallest track for very dense UIs; sm renders a narrower track; md meets the 44px touch-target minimum.

className.description: Additional CSS class names applied to the outermost wrapper element.

sizes.xs: track is 24px wide × 14px tall — very compact, for dense UIs. Well below 44px touch target.
sizes.sm: track is 32px wide × 18px tall — suitable for dense UIs. Below 44px touch target; avoid on touch-primary interfaces.
sizes.md: track is 44px wide × 24px tall — default. Wrapper meets 44px touch target via min-block-size.

do: Always provide a visible label (children) or aria-label so the toggle has an accessible name.
Use inside a FormControl when the toggle is part of a labelled form field group.
Use size='sm' only in dense UIs such as settings panels with many options.
dont: Do not use a Toggle for multi-step choices — use a Checkbox group or Radio group instead.
Do not rely on colour alone to communicate state — the thumb position must also signal on/off.
Do not apply inline styles — use the className prop and extend via CSS tokens.
